title.label: Airbnb is not how it used to be!

This was one of the most stressful travel experiences I’ve had. Airbnb allowed hosts to list rundown, smelly, poorly maintained apartments with no consequences.

I had to check out and leave in the middle of the night — twice — because the apartments were nothing like what was advertised. Despite this, Airbnb still charged me cancellation fees, even though the reason was clearly “apartment not as described.”

Airbnb failed to protect my rights as a customer and instead protected irresponsible hosts. This is unacceptable for a platform that charges high service fees but offers little real support when things go wrong.

title.label: System Failure to Protect Hosts & Enforce Policy

content.label:
As a long-time Superhost, I am profoundly disappointed with Airbnb's Community Support process. This app experience reflects a corporate system that has completely failed its partners.

The current support channel is rigid, inefficient, and fundamentally incapable of enforcing the platform’s own core policies. When faced with documented evidence of review manipulation, coercion, and factual dishonesty, the support team repeatedly refused to intervene, instead relying on automated filtering and providing canned responses.

Summary of Core System Failures:

AI-Driven Rejections: Cases involving policy violations (Extortion, Fraud) are automatically rejected without genuine manual review by a qualified agent, forcing users into endless support loops.
Failure to Protect Superhosts: The system prioritizes closing tickets over upholding fairness, allowing reviews based on documented lies and coercion to remain. This directly undermines the Superhost program and punishes the most valuable partners on the platform.
Policy Inaction: Support staff consistently fail to interpret and enforce policies such as the Extortion/Coercion Policy, even when presented with clear evidence of financial leverage attempts by guests.
This platform shows a blatant disregard for its partners and the integrity of the review system. If you are a host, be aware that you will not be protected when policies are clearly breached.

Immediate and urgent reform in policy enforcement and support procedure is required.

title.label: The policies to hosts are unfair and causing a lot of pain and suffering to our hosts.

content.label:
1. False reviews never get removed
Airbnb almost never deletes fake or misleading reviews, even when hosts provide clear evidence. It’s completely unfair and damaging to a host’s reputation.

2. Unreasonable penalties for cancellations
Even with valid or unavoidable reasons, hosts are fined $50 and their calendars get blocked. No real investigation, no empathy – just a cold, automated system.

3. Terrible support
Airbnb support works like a robot – scripted replies, no understanding of the actual problem, no real help. When you need them most, they’re silent

title.label: Deceptive Booking System & Unfair Host Penalties

content.label: I’m extremely disappointed with Airbnb’s deceptive practices. Their platform automatically accepted a guest booking while I was unavailable, without my approval. I had no choice but to cancel, which caused stress for both me and the guest—yet Airbnb fined me for it. To make matters worse, their support agent gave vague, unhelpful responses with no clear instructions on what documents to submit to appeal the penalty. She kept interrupting me on the phone, which made an already frustrating experience even worse. The whole experience was incredibly frustrating and unprofessional. I’ve already filed formal complaints with the FTC and BBB due to this issue. Hosts deserve transparency and control—Airbnb is failing on both. To other hosts, be cautious when you plan to host on Airbnb!

content.label: I had a terrible experience. The app’s customer service was awful, taking more than 48 hours to respond, and in the end, they only refunded me without helping me find a new place to stay. I received no support during that stressful time. Honestly, you’d be better off using Agoda
